entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Valerius Potitus Volusus was a consul in 410 BC and consular tribune in 415, 407, and 404 BC of the Roman Republic.

Born into a patrician family, Gaius Valerius Potitus Volusus rose through the ranks of Roman politics due to his family's influence and his own cunning. As a member of the aristocracy, he played a significant role in shaping Rome's governance during a period of turmoil and transformation.

Volusus' tenure as consul and tribune coincided with the Second Samnite War, a conflict that pitted the Roman Republic against the neighboring Samnite people. During this time, Volusus likely navigated the complexities of diplomacy and warfare, working to maintain Rome's dominance in the region.

The legacy of Gaius Valerius Potitus Volusus can be seen in the continued development of Roman governance structures and the expansion of Roman territories through military conquests. His influence on Roman politics also paved the way for future leaders who would shape the course of Roman history.

Gaius Valerius Potitus Volusus' life serves as a reminder of the complexities and nuances of ancient Roman politics, where family ties, personal ambition, and strategic alliances often determined the fate of individuals and nations.
